name: Oil-soaked long pole
description: A three-metre wooden pole slick with oil. Leave it until the oil soaks in, then wipe it down to work with it.
notes: Oiled state of a long pole; drawn in a darker wood than plain stock to show the soak. No glossy wet-wood finish exists, so the sheen is not shown. Hammering 1 follows the reference; it is a blunt pole, not a hammer, and could also serve as a reach weapon once melee is tuned.

name: Tonewood billet
description: A slab of slow-dried, close-grained wood set aside for building a stringed instrument. The ends are waxed to keep it from splitting.
notes: Spruce-coloured top billet with wax-sealed ends and a pencilled grade mark.

name: Tuning peg
description: A small wooden peg that holds an instrument string and turns to tighten it.
notes: Modelled as one friction peg 45 mm long, about 4 g. The reference gives 10 mm and 0.1 g, too small for any real peg, so the CHECK flags on mass, volume and length are deliberate. A stack of pegs shares the one model.

name: Heavy wooden beam
description: A massive squared timber, barely liftable by one person. Solid enough to build with, or saw down into planks and boards.
notes: 8 x 8 inch timber with a drying check along its top face.

name: Small wood block
description: A short square block of wood, a good size for carving small things.

name: Plywood sheet
description: A full four-by-eight sheet of plywood. Heavy and awkward to carry, but useful for boarding up and building once cut down to size.
notes: Drawn as three plies (birch faces, pine core) so the edge reads as plywood; the same model serves particle board or fibreboard sheets if they are added as variants.

name: Wooden post
description: A four-by-four post about the length of an arm span, the kind used for mailboxes and table legs.

name: Long wooden post
description: A long four-by-four post for framing walls and floors.

name: Short wooden post
description: A short length of four-by-four, about right for a chair or stool leg.
